newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Five Colombian rebels arrested over mayor's death.
newsitem.headline: Five Colombian rebels arrested over mayor's death.

text.p: Colombian police captured five leftist rebels on Friday who the authorities said had killed a small town mayor and were plotting to kill another.

The five members of the Popular Liberation Army, two of them minors, were arrested about 110 miles (180 km) west of Bogota for Sunday's shooting death of Climaco Navarro Palacio, mayor of Guatica in the coffee-growing region of Risaralda, police spokesmen said.
Navarro was the sixth mayor killed this year in Colombia, a country with one of the highest murder rates in the world. At least 20 mayors have been killed since January 1996.

The police spokesmen said Navarro had failed to pay rebel extortion money. An investigation following the arrests netted a confession and uncovered a second plot to kill the mayor of Mistrato, also in Risaralda.
In further violence, at least 10 people died in fighting in the northwest of the country on Thursday and early on Friday, military spokesmen said.
They said army troops fought into the early hours of Friday with members of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia, the country's largest rebel group.

One soldier was killed in the fighting and five civilians died when their hamlet on the outskirts of the town of Turbo was caught in the crossfire. Turbo is in the heart of the banana-growing province of Uraba in the northwest Antioquia province.

Four members of Colombia's second-largest leftist group, the National Liberation Army, died in a separate clash with a right-wing paramilitary group on the outskirts of the city of Remedios, which is also in Antioquia.
